newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot gas prices down across the board.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot gas prices down across the board.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices eased from last week in Wednesday trade with export points falling by the largest amounts, traders said.

Spot gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub was quoted at C$1.87/1.89 per gigajoule, down from C$1.93/1.98 last week, as mild western Canadian weather continued and NOVA conducted maintenance at Empress, Alberta.
The work, expected to be completed later Wednesday, served to trap some gas within the province, said a Calgary trader.
Gas for January delivery was talked at C$2.08/2.10 per GJ, up from C$2.00/2.05 on December 4.

Marketing sources were hard-pressed to gauge the direction of AECO prices over the next few days. "It will probably run sideways in the day market," the trader said. "There's more upside if (Empress) comes back to full service, but it's supposed to stay warm through the weekend."

Gas at the Huntington/Sumas point was discussed anywhere between US$2.75 and US$2.95 per million British thermal units, down from about US$3.50 last week. With warmer weather in the Pacific Northwest, most of the lessened demand was coming from California, said a Vancouver-based marketer.
Gas at Niagara, Ontario was quoted in the high US$3.70s, down 20 cents on the week. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
